`final class GlfwSnapshotWindow`<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.base.glfw.snapshot` · **Module:** `base-glfw` · **Source:** [GlfwSnapshotWindow.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/base/glfw/src/main/java/dev/joid/base/glfw/snapshot/GlfwSnapshotWindow.java)<br/>
**Backends:** <span class="joid-badge">LWJGL 3</span> <span class="joid-badge">Vulkan</span>

A hidden, undecorated GLFW window of a fixed size, on which the snapshot backends render.

## Description

It ships in the dev and demo jars of the backends; the published `joid-base-glfw` jar does not hold it.

## Learn more

- [Hidden windows](/build/base-modules/glfw/#hidden-windows)

## Creation details

<a id="GlfwSnapshotWindow-factory-create"></a>

### create

`GlfwSnapshotWindow create(int width, int height, Runnable hints)` <span class="joid-qualifier">factory</span>

**Throws:**

- `IllegalStateException`: GLFW cannot be initialized, check that the system has a display (DISPLAY or WAYLAND_DISPLAY on Linux)
- `IllegalStateException`: GLFW cannot create the …x… snapshot window, check that the graphics driver supports the graphics API the window asks for (its OpenGL version or Vulkan)

Initializes GLFW, runs `hints` to set the window hints of the backend, then creates a hidden window of that size in GLFW window coordinates; on a high-density macOS screen, its framebuffer is larger.
Throws an `IllegalStateException` when GLFW cannot start, often for lack of a display, or when the driver refuses the window.
